title: Lord, My Times Are in Thy Hand
description: Lord, My Times Are in Thy Hand in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 611 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Holy Contentment”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, my times are in thy hand: All my fond-est hopes have planned To thy wis-dom I re-sign, And would make thy pur-pose mine.

lines: Lord, my times are in thy hand:
All my fondest hopes have planned
And would make thy purpose mine.
Thou my daily task shalt give;
Day by day to thee I live:
Not my own, my Father's will.
O, to live exempt from care,
Strong in faith, with mind subdued,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
